findings.title: The 'read a migration by number, regex-extract its own pinned grammar, throw a matching never-edit-the-migration error' shape is written twice, 24 minutes apart, with no shared helper
findings.evidence: packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs's pinnedRoleCount() (commit 130ff25e, #867): `const stem = String(PIN_MIGRATION).padStart(4, "0") + "_"; const file = readdirSync(migrationsDir).find((f) => f.startsWith(stem)); ... const m = text.match(/rolname like 'clara%'\)\s*<>\s*(\d+)/); if (!m) { throw new Error(`${file} no longer carries the expected ... census assertion in the shape role-census-reset.mjs expects -- 0154 must never be edited; if this is a false alarm, update the regex here, never the migration.`); }`. scripts/check-document-region-field-paths.mjs's readFieldPathGrammar() (commit 9e3a8c1e, #857, written the same session immediately after): the identical shape -- locate a migration by numeric prefix, read its text, regex-extract several literals, and on mismatch `throw new Error(`${MIGRATION_REL} no longer carries clara._assert_field_path in the shape ... expects -- 0191 must never be edited; if this is a false alarm, update the three regexes here, never the migration.`)`. The second file's own header even names the first as its precedent ("the same posture packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs (#867) takes with migration 0154's pinned literal"), so the duplication is a conscious copy-adapt, not independent convergence.
findings.failure_scenario: A third ticket needing the same 'read one migration's own source as the single source of truth for a grammar, and fail loudly if that migration's shape ever moves' pattern will most likely paste a third copy rather than reach for a shared `readMigrationSource(number-or-stem)` + `assertShapeOrThrow(...)` helper -- and any future correction to this idiom (for example, tightening the not-found error to name the searched directory, which pinnedRoleCount already does and readFieldPathGrammar does not) has two call sites to update in step, with nothing to catch a lane that only updates one.
findings.required_fix: Not required for this wave; worth a follow-up extracting a small shared 'read a pinned migration by number and regex-extract its own asserted shape, or throw a standard never-edit-the-migration message' helper (e.g. in a small scripts-shared module) the next time a third check needs the same shape.

findings.title: isClaraRole() hand-restates, in JS, the exact 'clara%' predicate the SQL already encodes -- the one hand-kept copy in a file whose stated design principle is 'never a hand-kept copy'
findings.evidence: packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs: `export async function clusterClaraRoleCount(client) { const r = await client.query("select count(*)::int as n from pg_roles where rolname like 'clara%'"); return r.rows[0].n; }` and, added in the fix round (commit 6dea8f7a) a few lines below, `function isClaraRole(name) { return name.startsWith("clara"); }`, used in both check()'s subtraction and apply()'s drop loop specifically so they agree with clusterClaraRoleCount()'s own count. The file's own header and its pinnedRoleCount()/rolesMintedAfterPin() docstrings say three separate times that a value must be read from the migration source 'rather than duplicated by hand' / 'never a hand-kept copy' -- yet 'what counts as a clara role' is defined twice, once as SQL LIKE syntax and once as a JS startsWith, with nothing that would catch the two drifting apart (e.g. a future rename to a prefix the LIKE pattern would need escaping for but startsWith would not, such as a literal underscore).
findings.failure_scenario: A future change to the SQL predicate (say, escaping the LIKE pattern's own special characters, or narrowing it to `'clara\_%' escape '\\'`) would silently stop matching what isClaraRole() still accepts, so check()'s subtraction and apply()'s drop loop would disagree with clusterClaraRoleCount()'s own count -- exactly the class of arithmetic drift the fix round's own L04-S14 finding was about, reintroduced through the one predicate this file did not derive from a single source.
findings.required_fix: Not required for this wave; worth deriving isClaraRole() from the same literal the SQL query uses (a shared `const CLARA_ROLE_LIKE = "clara%"` string, translated once into both the SQL LIKE clause and a JS-equivalent matcher) the next time this file is touched, so there is one definition instead of two hand-synchronized ones.

findings.title: depLabel()'s nested ternary maps raw pg_shdepend.deptype single-letter codes inline, with no named lookup
findings.evidence: packages/db/scripts/role-census-reset.mjs: `function depLabel(row) { const kind = row.deptype === "a" ? "privilege" : row.deptype === "o" ? "ownership" : row.deptype === "m" ? "membership" : row.deptype; return `${row.datname} (${row.n} ${kind} dep${row.n === 1 ? "" : "s"})`; }`. The three-letter meaning of Postgres's own pg_shdepend.deptype catalog column ('a'/'o'/'m') lives only in this one inline ternary chain, with no named constant or lookup table a reader (or a second call site) could reuse or extend.
findings.failure_scenario: Low -- depLabel() has exactly one call site today (the log line in check()'s own loop and apply()'s refusal message), so this is a pure readability/extensibility observation, not a live defect: a reader has to know Postgres's pg_shdepend deptype vocabulary to decode the ternary, and a second caller needing the same mapping would either duplicate it or reach into this private function.
findings.required_fix: Not required; a small `DEPTYPE_LABELS = { a: "privilege", o: "ownership", m: "membership" }` object would read the same and survive a second call site without duplication, if one is ever added.

findings.title: The L04-S09 main()-exit-code self-test case stages and unstages a decoy fixture in this worktree's real git index, rather than an isolated interface
findings.evidence: scripts/check-document-region-field-paths.selftest.mjs, the 'main(): a REAL subprocess run exits non-zero...' case (added in commit 0b592123): it writes a decoy file at `packages/db/tests/__check857_selftest_decoy.mjs` inside THIS worktree, runs `execFileSync("git", ["add", "--", DECOY_REL], { cwd: SELFTEST_ROOT })` to stage it (because `scanTargetFiles()` reads `git ls-files`, which only sees the INDEX), spawns the real script as a subprocess, then in a `finally` runs `git reset --quiet HEAD -- <path>` and deletes the file. This is a legitimate way to exercise the tool's actual dependency (git ls-files) rather than mocking it, and I confirmed `git status --porcelain` is clean immediately after a real run of this file -- but it is a side effect on the lane's own shared git index rather than a fully self-contained interface, and a hard process kill between the `git add` and the `finally` (not caught by try/catch) would leave a staged decoy file in this worktree's real index for the next command to trip over.
findings.failure_scenario: An interrupted CI run or a killed node process landing between the `execFileSync("git", ["add", ...])` call and the `finally` block would leave `packages/db/tests/__check857_selftest_decoy.mjs` staged (though never committed) in this lane's own worktree, surfacing as an unexplained `git status` entry the next person to touch this worktree has to notice and unstage by hand.
findings.required_fix: Not required -- the risk window is small (synchronous code between two adjacent statements) and self-contained to this lane's own worktree, never another lane's. If this pattern is copied to a second check script, consider whether the target repo state (staged-in-index) can be swapped for a disposable git working tree (`git worktree add` into a temp dir) so a kill mid-test cannot leave the lane's real index dirty.
